title: Heavy-tailed stationary behaviour of SGD on neural-network losses
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Simsekli et al. observed that SGD gradient noise in deep networks is heavy-tailed, and Gurbuzbalaban, Simsekli and Zhu proved for linear regression that the SGD iterates converge to a stationary law with power-law tails whose index alpha decreases as eta/b (step over batch) grows. The same paper states a criterion for nonlinear recursions (its Theorem 1, Mirek-type asymptotically linear random maps). Verify it for a concrete nonlinear model: e.g. constant-step SGD with batch b on a generalized linear model or a two-layer network with a smooth bounded activation, Gaussian inputs and persistent label noise. Prove that the iterates have a stationary law, that the recursion contracts on average and is asymptotically linear with a non-arithmetic multiplier and a nonzero tail constant, so that the stationary tail is a power law with index given by the Lyapunov equation, with alpha < 2 in a nonempty range of (eta, b).
statement_caveat: For linear regression the result follows from Kesten's theory of random affine recursions; nonlinear networks give non-affine random iterations. Monotonicity of the index in eta/b is proved under Gaussian data (assumption A3) and alpha >= 1 (auditor codex-w687, 16 Oct).
source: M. Gurbuzbalaban, U. Simsekli and L. Zhu, The Heavy-Tail Phenomenon in SGD, arXiv:2006.04740 (2020); U. Simsekli, L. Sagun and M. Gurbuzbalaban, A Tail-Index Analysis of Stochastic Gradient Noise in Deep Neural Networks, arXiv:1901.06053 (2019)
locator: 2006.04740 Theorem 1 (PDF p4); Theorems 2-4 and Proposition 5 (PDF pp7-8). Read by codex-w687, 16 Oct.
why_important: Heavy tails change what 'SGD finds' (Lévy-driven rather than Brownian exploration) and have been tied to generalization; a theorem for nonlinear models would turn an empirical claim into probability.
where_it_stands: Linear case proved; nonlinear results under strong assumptions only (to verify). Open in general.
note: Fame: connects SGD to Kesten's random recursion theory; widely cited line.

audit.status_ref: arXiv:2006.04740, Theorem 1 (Mirek-type nonlinear recursions), PDF p4; Theorems 2-4 and Proposition 5, PDF pp7-8
audit.statement_ok: NO: specify nonlinear model, loss, sample law, persistent label noise, recurrence/contraction assumptions and tail observable; without these a stationary distribution need not exist, nor be heavy-tailed
audit.replace_with: Choose a concrete nonlinear regression law and prove average contraction, asymptotic linearity, a nonarithmetic multiplier and a nondegenerate tail constant before asking for the tail index.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: a scalar smooth bounded perturbation of linear regression may satisfy the already-stated Mirek criterion; verify all recurrence and tail-nondegeneracy hypotheses explicitly.
audit.locator: 2006.04740 Section 3.1 Theorem 1, PDF p4; Section 3.2 Theorems 2-4 and Proposition 5, PDF pp7-8; 1901.06053 Section 5 Conclusion and Open Problems, PDF pp10-11

title: Edge universality for the conjugate kernel of a random network
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Conjugate kernel of a one-layer random network: Y = sigma(W X / sqrt d), W m x d with iid N(0, 1) entries, X d x N with iid sub-Gaussian entries (or columns uniform on the sphere of radius sqrt d), m, d, N tending to infinity proportionally. Take sigma Lipschitz (or smooth), centred, with no linear part: E sigma(Z) = 0 and E Z sigma(Z) = 0 for Z ~ N(0, 1). Prove that lambda_max(Y Y^T / N) converges to the right edge of the limiting (Pennington-Worah) law, which is regular there, with Tracy-Widom (beta = 1) fluctuations on the n^(-2/3) scale. Then allow a linear component, which changes the bulk: state an explicit rule for any finite-rank spikes it or the input design creates and prove the same edge statement for the largest eigenvalue after them. For polynomial activations of degree at least 3 the top eigenvalue at widths below several thousand is an outlier made by the largest entry of Y, so the statement is asymptotic only.
statement_caveat: The global law is known; the edge and fluctuations are the open part. Outliers come from the mean and the linear Hermite component of sigma.
source: L. Benigni and S. Péché, Eigenvalue distribution of nonlinear models of random matrices, arXiv:1904.03090 (2019); Z. Fan and Z. Wang, Spectra of the Conjugate Kernel and Neural Tangent Kernel for linear-width neural networks, arXiv:2005.11879 (2020)
locator: to verify: open questions at the end of Fan–Wang and Benigni–Péché.
why_important: Nonlinear random matrices are a new class of random-matrix models born from neural networks; edge behaviour governs conditioning of random-feature regression.
where_it_stands: Global laws proved; edge results partial (to verify). Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: nonlinear random matrix theory is an active RMT topic since Pennington–Worah 2017.

audit.status_ref: Benigni-Peche1904.03090 Theorems2.2/2.3 PDF p5, fully read with iid-entry,strong-tail,analyticity and centering hypotheses p4, prove the global law. Remark2.5 p5 explicitly states that their method also gives largest-eigenvalue convergence for odd activations. Fan-Wang2005.11879 Assumption3.2/Theorem3.4 PDF p5, fully read with definition p4, proves CK bulk convergence and bounded norm under approximately orthogonal inputs and smooth centered normalized activation. Footnote2 p4 explicitly warns bulk weak convergence does not imply individual-edge convergence. Neither opened result proves the requested broad Tracy-Widom law.
audit.statement_ok: NO: iid columns alone do not imply the quoted global law or bounded edge. Specify input distribution/concentration,moments,activation regularity/normalization,aspect ratios,regular edge,scaling constant and a precise finite-rank spike rule. The linear Hermite component generally affects the bulk and cannot simply be labeled an outlier to discard.
audit.replace_with: Fix iid sub-Gaussian entries or a specified concentrated input design and a smooth centered activation, remove only explicitly identified finite-rank spikes, then ask edge rigidity/Tracy-Widom at a nondegenerate right edge. Compare later largest-eigenvalue results before claiming an open case.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: isotropic iid-column radial counterexample completed in T248_radial_diagnostic.md. A Gaussian polynomial-activation regular-edge special case is concrete, but no novelty clearance.
audit.locator: 1904.03090 Sec2 assumptions PDF p4;Theorems2.2/2.3 and Remark2.5 p5.2005.11879 Definition3.1/footnote2 p4;Assumption3.2 and Theorem3.4 p5;NTK extension Theorem3.7 p7. Exact generic Tracy-Widom conjecture is not located in these source passages.

title: Convergence of Adam with the hyperparameters used in practice
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Reddi, Kale and Kumar construct convex problems where Adam with fixed beta_1, beta_2 diverges. Zhang et al. show Adam converges to a neighbourhood of stationary points for smooth nonconvex objectives when beta_2 is chosen large depending on the problem (after beta_1, n are fixed). Prove (or disprove) that Adam with beta_1 < sqrt(beta_2), beta_2 close to 1 independent of the problem, and a decaying or small constant step size, converges to stationary points on smooth nonconvex finite-sum objectives under standard noise assumptions, and explain the empirical advantage of Adam over SGD on transformer losses in a provable model.
statement_caveat: Many partial results (problem-dependent hyperparameters, bounded gradients, affine noise) exist.
source: S. J. Reddi, S. Kale and S. Kumar, On the Convergence of Adam and Beyond, arXiv:1904.09237 (2019); Y. Zhang, C. Chen, N. Shi, R. Sun and Z.-Q. Luo, Adam Can Converge Without Any Modification On Update Rules, arXiv:2208.09632 (2022)
locator: to verify: Zhang et al., the discussion of problem-dependent beta_2.
why_important: Adam trains nearly every large model; its convergence in the regime used is still not established.
note: Fame: Reddi et al. was an ICLR 2018 best paper.

title: Overconfidence of overparameterized classifiers
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Bai, Mei, Wang and Xiong prove that logistic regression fitted by maximum likelihood in the proportional regime (n, d → ∞, n/d fixed) is overconfident: its predicted probabilities exceed the true conditional probabilities, even without overparameterization. Prove a comparable theorem for a two-layer network trained by gradient descent on cross-entropy in a solvable regime (random features, or mean-field with a single-index teacher): characterize the calibration error as a function of n/d, width and training time, and show whether early stopping yields calibration.
statement_caveat: Empirical overconfidence of modern networks is well documented (Guo et al. 2017); theory is limited to linear and random-features models (to verify).
source: Y. Bai, S. Mei, H. Wang and C. Xiong, Don't Just Blame Over-parametrization for Over-confidence: Theoretical Analysis of Calibration in Binary Classification, arXiv:2102.07856 (2021)
locator: to verify: Bai et al., conclusion (networks as open).
why_important: Calibrated probabilities are what make a classifier's confidence usable; it is a question about the limiting law of a trained predictor's outputs.
where_it_stands: Open for networks as far as the writer knows.

title: Catastrophic forgetting under random task orderings
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: In continual linear regression, a model is fit (by gradient descent to convergence, i.e. projection) on a sequence of T tasks, each a consistent linear system in R^d, cycling or sampling tasks from a fixed collection. Evron et al. bound the forgetting (loss on earlier tasks after k steps) and show it can be arbitrarily bad for adversarial orderings but decays for cyclic and random orderings. Determine the optimal worst-case rate of forgetting after k iterations under uniformly random task ordering, as a function of k (independent of d and of the task similarity), with matching lower bounds.
statement_caveat: Evron et al. give a rate for random orderings with dimension dependence; dimension-free rates were later obtained in part (to verify 2024-25 work, e.g. on the connection with Kaczmarz methods and random products of projections).
source: I. Evron, E. Moroshko, R. Ward, N. Srebro and D. Soudry, How catastrophic can catastrophic forgetting be in linear regression?, arXiv:2205.09588 (2022)
locator: to verify: Evron et al., open questions on random orderings.
why_important: It is the solvable model of continual learning, and reduces to products of random projections (random Kaczmarz) — a probability problem.
where_it_stands: Possibly partly solved since; to verify.

title: Adaptive edge of stability: the preconditioned sharpness
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Cohen et al. observe that full-batch adaptive methods run at an adaptive edge of stability: the top eigenvalue of the preconditioned Hessian P^(-1) H settles near the threshold 38/eta for Adam with beta1 = 0.9, while the raw sharpness keeps growing. With a fixed epsilon the preconditioned sharpness is at most |H|/epsilon, so epsilon must shrink with eta. For a randomly initialized rank-one or diagonal quadratic or deep linear model, full-batch Adam (or RMSProp) with stated betas, bias correction and epsilon = epsilon(eta) tending to 0 at a stated rate, prove that after a burn-in the preconditioned sharpness, or the curvature along the active direction, rises to and stays within o(1/eta) of the threshold while the loss decreases non-monotonically; characterize when the active-direction curvature rather than the top sharpness tracks the threshold.
statement_caveat: Gradient-descent EoS has partial proofs (self-stabilization, compare T226); the adaptive version is open (to verify).
source: J. M. Cohen, B. Ghorbani, S. Krishnan, N. Agarwal, S. Medapati, M. Badura, D. Suo, D. Cardoze, Z. Nado, G. E. Dahl and J. Gilmer, Adaptive Gradient Methods at the Edge of Stability, arXiv:2207.14484 (2022)
locator: to verify: Cohen et al., conclusion.
why_important: Adam trains essentially all large models; its stability regime decides what learning rates work.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: widely cited follow-up to the EoS paper (ICLR 2021).

audit.status_ref: Cohen et al.2207.14484 AppendixA.1 Lemma2 PDF p14, fully read with recurrence, gives the frozen EMA-heavy-ball quadratic threshold 2*(1+beta1)/(eta*(1-beta1)),38/eta at beta1=.9; the adaptive-Adam claim is empirical. Fong-Yang2608.20638 Proposition3.1 and Theorems3.2/3.3 PDF pp5-6, fully opened, prove an exact rank-one 2-cycle and finite regime-exit/crossing statements under w_max>2 and, with momentum,beta2>beta1^2. These are partial rigorous adaptive EoS results, not eventual top-eigenvalue O(eta^c) attraction for general networks. Additional2608.20638 Theorems3.4/3.5 PDF p7 fully opened: diagonal-quadratic Adam active-curvature alternatives and general C2 bounded-Hessian gradient-coercive nondegenerate-stationary RMSProp active-curvature crossings around2 up to C_f epsilon/eta, with never-finitely-stationary assumption. These do not give the row uniform eventual eta^c band for Adam; raw inactive-direction sharpness has a source counterexample.
audit.statement_ok: NO: quantify the data/model, initialization, beta parameters, bias correction, epsilon relative to eta, probability and time interval. Fixed epsilon and bounded Hessian preclude attraction to a threshold diverging as1/eta for all small eta. Distinguish frozen stability from adaptive dynamics and maximum sharpness from active directional curvature.
audit.replace_with: Choose random-initialized rank-one or diagonal quadratic/deep-linear model and specify epsilon/eta scaling, burn-in and observable. Improve a particular theorem from the2026 rank-one analysis or characterize when active curvature, rather than top sharpness, tracks the threshold.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: frozen-threshold and epsilon-regime diagnostic completed in T421_threshold_diagnostic.md. Generic top-sharpness attraction for nonlinear networks is a PROGRAMME.
audit.locator: 2207.14484 empirical statement PDF p1;fixed/adaptive preconditioning p3;AppendixA.1 Lemma2 p14.2608.20638 definitions/rank-one reduction and Proposition3.1/Theorem3.2 p5,Theorem3.3 p6;sharpness-directional distinction pp6-7.
